newsitem.title: CANADA: Golden Rule shares continue slide.
newsitem.headline: Golden Rule shares continue slide.

text.p: Golden Rule Resources Ltd shares continued to tumble on Tuesday, as investors gave in to their doubts about the exploration company's gold prospect in Ghana, analysts said.
The stock slumped 0.85 to 7.25 on almost 700,000 shares by midday on the Toronto Stock Exchange.

Golden Rule has slid steadily since it peaked at 13.10 on January 27. The stock has fallen as quickly as it climbed, rising from C$5.25 on January 6, where it was trading before the company released trenching results from Ghana.

Golden Rule released a second set of trenching results from its Stenpad property last week, extending mineralization to 96.3 metres grading 16.0 grams of gold per tonne of ore, from previous results showing 87 metres grading 15.9 grams per tonne.
While analysts said the results were positive, the stock has declined steadily since then.
"It's just the same factors driving it down that drove it up in the first place," a Golden Rule spokeswoman said in a phone interview from Calgary.
She said the company had not had any bad news recently.
